mechanisms.name: formation of protective rutile oxide scale

evidence.quote: Cr10 exhibits much slower oxidation kinetics compared with Al10, attributed to i) the dominant rutile-type Ti1–2x(Nb,Ta)xCrxO2 oxide that has lower volume mismatch with the alloy matrix compared with (Nb,Ta)2O5, as indicated by low Pilling-Bedworth ratio (PBR) values of 1.03–1.76; and ii) the alternative layer structure consisting of dense rutile and porous mixed oxides that is conducive to prohibiting stress cumulation and cracking.

mechanisms.name: formation of mixed oxide scale with voids and cracks

evidence.quote: The oxide scale of Cr10 after 800°C-1 h oxidation features an alternative layer structure consisting of dense rutile Ti1–2x(Nb,Ta)xCrxO2 layer and porous mixed oxides (Ti1–2x(Nb,Ta)xCrxO2 + (Nb,Ta)2O5) layer, whereas Al10 exhibit a single mixed oxide scale (Ti1–2x(Nb,Ta)xAlxO2 + (Nb,Ta)2O5) containing lots of voids and cracks.

Cr10 exhibits much slower oxidation kinetics compared with Al10, attributed to i) the dominant rutile-type Ti1–2x(Nb,Ta)xCrxO2 oxide that has lower volume mismatch with the alloy matrix compared with (Nb,Ta)2O5, as indicated by low Pilling-Bedworth ratio (PBR) values of 1.03–1.76; and ii) the alternative layer structure consisting of dense rutile and porous mixed oxides that is conducive to prohibiting stress cumulation and cracking.

The oxide scale of Cr10 after 800°C-1 h oxidation features an alternative layer structure consisting of dense rutile Ti1–2x(Nb,Ta)xCrxO2 layer and porous mixed oxides (Ti1–2x(Nb,Ta)xCrxO2 + (Nb,Ta)2O5) layer, whereas Al10 exhibit a single mixed oxide scale (Ti1–2x(Nb,Ta)xAlxO2 + (Nb,Ta)2O5) containing lots of voids and cracks.

Cr10 exhibits much slower oxidation kinetics compared with Al10, attributed to i) the dominant rutile-type Ti1–2x(Nb,Ta)xCrxO2 oxide that has lower volume mismatch with the alloy matrix compared with (Nb,Ta)2O5, as indicated by low Pilling-Bedworth ratio (PBR) values of 1.03–1.76; and ii) the alternative layer structure consisting of dense rutile and porous mixed oxides that is conducive to prohibiting stress cumulation and cracking.

The structural differences of oxides, i.e., the alternative layer oxides in Cr10 versus the mixed oxides in Al10, are influenced by both formation energies and volume fractions of oxides. Voids and cracks in oxide scales are induced by oxide-alloy and oxide-oxide volume mismatches that can be quantified by Pilling-Bedworth ratio (PBR). More cracks in the oxide scale of Al10 compared with Cr10 should attribute to the higher volume fraction of (Nb,Ta)2O5 of larger PBR values.
